title: 07. Advanced & Agentic RAG: What Is MCP?
summary: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard protocol developed by Anthropic (2024) that defines how AI models (LLMs) communicate with external tools, data sources, and services in a standardized, secure, and interoperable way.

sections.title: 1.1 Definition & Core Concept
sections.body:
**MCP (Model Context Protocol)** is an **open standard protocol** developed by **Anthropic** (2024) that defines how AI models (LLMs) communicate with external tools, data sources, and services in a **standardized, secure, and interoperable** way.

> **Simple Analogy:** MCP is like **USB-C for AI** — just as USB-C is a universal connector that works with any device, MCP is a universal connector that lets any AI model talk to any tool/data source without custom integrations.

sections.title: 1.2 The Problem MCP Solves
sections.body:
### ❌ Before MCP — The Old Way (The Problem)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    BEFORE MCP (Chaos)                           │
│                                                                 │
│  App 1 ──custom code──► Tool A                                  │
│  App 1 ──custom code──► Tool B                                  │
│  App 1 ──custom code──► Database C                              │
│                                                                 │
│  App 2 ──different custom code──► Tool A  (duplicate work!)     │
│  App 2 ──different custom code──► Tool B  (duplicate work!)     │
│                                                                 │
│  Problems:                                                      │
│  ❌ N×M integrations needed (N apps × M tools)                  │
│  ❌ No standard security model                                   │
│  ❌ Each integration breaks separately                           │
│  ❌ No context management standard                               │
│  ❌ Vendor lock-in                                               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### ✅ After MCP — The Solution

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    AFTER MCP (Unified)                          │
│                                                                 │
│  App 1 ──MCP──► MCP Server A (Tool A)                          │
│  App 2 ──MCP──► MCP Server A (Tool A)  ← Same server!          │
│  App 3 ──MCP──► MCP Server A (Tool A)  ← Reusable!             │
│                                                                 │
│  Benefits:                                                      │
│  ✅ N+M integrations only (N apps + M servers)                  │
│  ✅ Standardized security (OAuth 2.0, API keys)                  │
│  ✅ Universal context management                                 │
│  ✅ Any LLM + Any Tool = Works!                                  │
│  ✅ One MCP server, many clients                                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: 1.4 MCP Communication Flow
sections.body:
```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   MCP REQUEST LIFECYCLE                               │
│                                                                       │
│  USER: "What's the weather in NYC?"                                   │
│         │                                                             │
│         ▼                                                             │
│  ┌─────────────┐                                                      │
│  │  LLM/Claude │  1. Receives user message                            │
│  │             │  2. Decides: "I need weather tool"                   │
│  └──────┬──────┘                                                      │
│         │  tool_call: {name: "get_weather", args: {city: "NYC"}}      │
│         ▼                                                             │
│  ┌─────────────┐                                                      │
│  │  MCP Client │  3. Translates to JSON-RPC request                   │
│  │             │  4. Sends via transport (stdio/SSE/HTTP)             │
│  └──────┬──────┘                                                      │
│         │  JSON-RPC: {method: "tools/call", params: {...}}            │
│         ▼                                                             │
│  ┌─────────────┐                                                      │
│  │  MCP Server │  5. Receives request                                 │
│  │             │  6. Executes get_weather("NYC")                      │
│  │             │  7. Returns result                                   │
│  └──────┬──────┘                                                      │
│         │  Result: {temperature: 72, condition: "Sunny"}              │
│         ▼                                                             │
│  ┌─────────────┐                                                      │
│  │  MCP Client │  8. Returns result to LLM                            │
│  └──────┬──────┘                                                      │
│         ▼                                                             │
│  ┌─────────────┐                                                      │
│  │  LLM/Claude │  9. "It's 72°F and Sunny in NYC!"                   │
│  └─────────────┘                                                      │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
